item.title: Desk 1.0.20
item.description: Triage New in stacks (who needs you, each client, colleagues, people, notifications, money) from Home or above the list, and teach Desk where mail belongs. Everything at the top of Folders shows every email with where it is. Folders are tidier: the ones you use up top, the rest under More, mute and hide, and Tidy Up Folders to remove empty ones. Rules for several senders now run in Gmail.

item.title: Desk 1.0.19
item.description: Fixes a freeze that could happen while scrolling a long conversation. Forwarded emails now show the email that was forwarded, even when nothing was added. People's photos now show when they write from another of their addresses.

item.title: Desk 1.0.18
item.description: Smoother everywhere. The mail list is rebuilt natively, so it scrolls at your display's full rate (120 Hz on ProMotion Macs), and switching between New, To Do, Waiting and the rest is instant. Opening an email (and pressing D for Done) no longer stalls, long conversations open quickly, and Mail, Calendar, search and Home all respond faster.

item.title: Desk 1.0.17
item.description: Home: with no email open, Desk shows your day at a glance: your next meeting and what's open with those people, the shape of your day, who's waiting on your reply, who you're waiting on, what comes back today, your clients this week, and what's done. Sending a reply takes you back there; so do the new Home button, Esc and Shift-Command-H.

item.title: Desk 1.0.16
item.description: Night Sky's northern lights now shine across the top of the window and between the panels, where you can see them. New to Desk? Setup now also asks what you'd like to be notified about.

item.title: Desk 1.0.15
item.description: A new Night Sky backdrop: stars, the Milky Way, northern lights and a still lake (Settings › Appearance › Scenes). New to Desk? A short setup now walks you through adding your email accounts, choosing light or dark and your backdrop, text size, and your meeting hours.

item.title: Desk 1.0.14
item.description: Conversations read like conversations: newest first, every email open showing only what's new, repeated signatures folded to one line, day dividers and reply times, whose turn it is, and replies written above the conversation. Wide screens get a side column with people, the summary (now with open questions and decisions), tasks, files and your next meeting. The button beside Mail/Calendar becomes New, Reply or Send. Undo-send moves to the top right, and notices are solid.

item.title: Desk 1.0.13
item.description: The mail list starts at the top when you open it and stays there as mail arrives, with a Top button when you're far down. On a call, its people stay when the meeting runs over, and finding a time with them is a switch you turn on. Right-click an event to find a time with its guests.

item.title: Desk 1.0.12
item.description: Meeting notifications with a Join button, now shown even while Desk is open, with a choice of how early and which calendars (Settings › Calendar). Join right from the Mail sidebar's timeline. On a call, Clear no longer loses people: Show Everyone brings the whole call back.

item.title: Desk 1.0.11
item.description: Desk now carries its own SQLite, so every Mac runs the same database engine. Smoother scrolling in the mail list. In the calendar, clicking an event shows its details again (double-click to edit), and a meeting that's on more than one of your calendars is marked, with each copy one click away.

item.title: Desk 1.0.10
item.description: Fixes empty New, To Do, Waiting, Later and Done on macOS 26 after 1.0.9. Your mail was never affected.

item.title: Desk 1.0.9
item.description: Folders button with unread counts and Mark Read for every folder; choose New or Updates for any sender (right-click); a refresh button, and Desk checks for mail when you switch to it; sign-in links and codes always land in New.

item.title: Desk 1.0.8
item.description: Conversations open at the top. Click a conversation's count to see each email in the list and jump straight to one. Today, Next week and Later sit at the top of the strip for easier dragging. The right-click menu shows each shortcut key. Fixes working hours showing an hour off on days the clocks change.

item.title: Desk 1.0.7
item.description: Fixes curly quotes and dashes in email sent from Outlook showing as garbled characters (like youâ€™d); email already affected is repaired. Choose which calendars count toward your availability: click the clock beside a calendar (off unless you turn it on). Cleared calendar activity now stays cleared on all your Macs, and clearing a meeting keeps guests' later answers out of the activity. A Settings gear at the top right. Fixes settings disappearing when another Mac was on an older version.

item.title: Desk 1.0.6
item.description: Calendar's sidebar groups your calendars by account on cards you can fold up, with one Add Calendar menu for subscriptions, your Mac's calendars and new accounts. Account logos now show in the message list, the From menu when writing, and the calendar sidebar. Fixes Calendar's sidebar being cut off and the mail list opening too narrow in 1.0.5, while keeping quick switching. One search bar for Mail and Calendar, and no Mail count on the switcher.

item.title: Desk 1.0.5
item.description: A floating Mail/Calendar bar with counts and a quick New Message / New Event button. Accounts show their logo: company, Gmail, iCloud, Outlook, or your own image (Settings › Accounts). Make text bigger or smaller everywhere (Settings › Appearance, or ⌘+ / ⌘−). Easier to read: more solid panels (choose Glassy, Balanced or Solid), clearer popovers and darker event text. Switching between Mail and Calendar is about twice as fast. Client emoji now sits beside the sender. Fixes a crash when switching from Month view to Day or Week.

item.title: Desk 1.0.4
item.description: Calendars from all your accounts (Google and iCloud), invitations to answer pinned until you reply, calendar colors and options, subscribed calendars, out of office and focus time, travel time and leave-now alerts, Send Later, missing-attachment warning, report spam and block sender, and your accounts follow you to other Macs through iCloud Keychain.

item.title: Desk 1.0.3
item.description: Photos of the people who email you and logos for companies' no-reply mail. Reply All and Forward beside Reply. With Desk on more than one Mac, rules run on just one of them. Clearer account buttons, a more visible image banner, and trusted image senders sync between your Macs.

item.title: Desk 1.0.2
item.description: Calendar email moves out of your inbox into a Calendar activity feed, where you can answer invitations and open recordings and notes. Each meeting shows its files, links and who answered. Click anyone for their files, links, meetings and emails. People, pins, templates, signatures, rules and settings now sync between your Macs through iCloud.

item.title: Desk 1.0.1
item.description: Sign in with Google straight away on new Macs — no setup file needed.

item.title: Desk 1.0.0
item.description: First release: mail from all your accounts in five places (New, To Do, Waiting, Later, Done), your calendar with time zones and free times for the people you meet with, and on-device AI.
